summary.allegation: The cardholder says Roastline Coffee Co charged them twice for GBP 54.00 on 12 April 2025 and that only one purchase was made, so the second charge is a duplicate.
summary.to_defend: Visa requires evidence that the two GBP 54.00 charges were two separate purchases, with separate purchase documentation and distinct timestamps and authorisation codes for each.

requirements.title: Two separate purchases
requirements.text: Evidence the two transactions are for two separate purchases (e.g. different order IDs, different items, different services rendered).
requirements.finding: The two invoices show different order IDs (RL-ORDER-44188 and RL-ORDER-44192), different invoice numbers and entirely different baskets: coffee beans on the first order and an Aeropress Go kit with filter papers on the second.

requirements.title: Each purchase documented
requirements.text: Documentation of each purchase event (separate invoices, separate delivery confirmations, separate service dates).
requirements.finding: Each purchase has its own invoice and its own delivery record: invoice RL-88291 delivered 14 April 2025 on DPD consignment 7711224488, and invoice RL-88294 delivered 15 April 2025 on DPD consignment 7711224501.

requirements.title: Timestamps and auth codes
requirements.text: Transaction timestamps and authorisation codes for each charge.
requirements.finding: Distinct capture timestamps and authorisation codes are recorded for each charge: auth 442189 captured at 08:11:33 on 12 April 2025 and auth 552781 captured at 19:42:18 the same day, the first matching transaction txn_5523IJ.

alerts.text: D1 states the capture as 12 Apr 2025 08:11:33 BST while the transaction record shows 2025-04-12T08:11:33Z (UTC), so the clock time is identical but the time zone label differs by an hour; confirm which time base the merchant's invoices use.

reasons: Every requirement the decision relies on is backed by verified evidence

checks.label: Key evidence comes from document text, not only from an image
Images the evidence relies on are fully legible
Every quoted passage was found in the documents
The disputed charge matches the merchant's own records
The rule check and the AI recommendation agree

justification: Represent: R1 is decisive, the two GBP 54.00 charges carry different order IDs and completely different items, and R2 and R3 are also satisfied by separate invoices, deliveries and authorisation codes.
rationale:
The cardholder was charged GBP 54.00 twice on 12 April 2025 because two separate orders were placed that day, not because one purchase was processed twice.
Order RL-ORDER-44188 (invoice RL-88291) was for Ethiopia Yirgacheffe and House Espresso beans totalling GBP 60.00 less a GBP 6.00 loyalty discount, authorised under code 442189 at 08:11:33 on 12 April 2025.
Order RL-ORDER-44192 (invoice RL-88294) was for an Aeropress Go starter kit and filter papers totalling GBP 54.00, authorised under a different code 552781 at 19:42:18 on the same day.
The two orders shipped on separate DPD consignments, 7711224488 delivered 14 April 2025 and 7711224501 delivered 15 April 2025, to the cardholder's address at N1 4PD.
The disputed transaction carried AVS match Y, CVV match M and a frictionless 3DS result, and the identical amounts are coincidental rather than evidence of duplicate processing.
analyst_notes: Ask the merchant for DPD proof of delivery or signature scans for consignments 7711224488 and 7711224501 to back the invoice delivery lines.
Confirm with the merchant whether invoice times are stated in BST or UTC before filing, given the 08:11:33 label difference against the transaction record.
